why: Figure B is made of two copies of figure A: on the left a copy turned upside down (flipped top to bottom), and on the right the same figure A. Do the same with C: on the left C flipped upside down, so the dot is at the top and the zigzag arrow points down, and on the right the normal C. Only option 5 keeps the full zigzag on both arrow heads. Option 1 loses the zigzag on the left figure, and options 3 and 4 have only half of the zigzag.
trick: When the second figure has two parts, check if it is 'flipped copy + original copy'. Then compare small details like the wings of the arrow.
note: Option figures are small in the scan; exact zigzag details of the wrong options 1-4 are approximated, but option 5 is the only one with both full zigzags.
